messages.author: c30f454051765351
messages.subject: Re: Today's SDM quiz
parts:
Probably too simple an explanation, by my gut reaction is because there are more data being used to estimate the slopes in the abundance model, so detection bias doesn’t become an all or nothing scenario as it is in p/a. So, the slopes can still be estimated in an abundance model even under p<1.

 

--

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: Today's SDM quiz
parts:
I would say it's because the contamination is one-sided with presence/absence data, which causes the effect size to be underestimated on average.  With abundance, the imperfect detection is an equal opportunity phenomenon so the relative comparisons still hold.  The stark difference in accuracy/precision also highlights how hungry the logistic regression is for data, and the greater relative value of counts over 0/1s.

I bet that even if you model p, the occupancy slopes will be slightly underestimated.

messages.author: f2d11dcac04fbaea
messages.subject: Re: Today's SDM quiz
parts:
Dear Marc,

Using the following rough idea, my collaborator has shown that the difference may be responsible for the link functions of two models:

If there are many sample replicates at each site, so that the detection probability (p) can be treated as a known parameter, we can simply consider the following equation for both N-mixture and occupancy model:
   link(Y[i] *p) = a + b * X[i] + e[i],
where Y[i] = abundance/occupancy, X[i] = covariate, a = intercept, b = slope and e[i] = error term (Poisson or binomial). link( ) represents the link function.

Assuming the covariate has unit variance (without loss of generality), the slope is the covariance of link(Y[i]*p) and X[i]. Thus, the bias of the slope (Δb) is given by
   Δb = cov(link(Y[i]*p), X[i]) - cov(link(Y[i]), X[i])
      = cov(link(Y[i]*p)-link(Y[i]), X[i]).
The link function is then substituted into the above equation:
N mixture (link = log)
   Δb = cov(log(p), X[i]) = 0.
Occupancy (link = logit)
   Δb = cov(log(1-Y[i]), X[i]) - cov(log(1-Y[i]*p), X[i]) ≠ 0.
Therefore, the slope estimates of occupancy model can be affected by the detection probability.

Best wishes,
Yuichi
